object_context: Conditional blow-up-classification atom for the unforced whole-space 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes Clay statement (A): assume a finite-time Type-I singularity in a suitable weak continuation of smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free data and characterize the parabolically rescaled limit strongly enough to reach a valid Liouville/rigidity contradiction. This atom does not cover Type-II concentration.
structural_coordinates: local suitable-weak-solution structure and local energy inequality near a candidate singular point
scale-invariant Type-I control through local velocity/gradient/pressure quantities, bounded rather than necessarily small
parabolic blow-up extraction with spatial translation, temporal translation, and scaling noncompactness
ancient time domain (-infinity,0) after rescaling a finite-time singularity
mild bounded ancient solution target class arising in the Albritton–Barker Type-I equivalence
renormalized-flow orbit type: exact self-similar=fixed point, discretely self-similar=periodic orbit, general Type-I ancient solution=broader complete trajectory
nonlocal pressure and far-field behavior must survive localization/rescaling

equivalent_formulations: Albritton–Barker Type-I equivalence: a suitable weak solution has a Type-I singular point if and only if there exists a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution satisfying their registered Type-I decay condition I<infinity.

Under logarithmic self-similar coordinates around a putative blow-up time, exact backward self-similarity becomes stationarity of the rescaled trajectory, discrete self-similarity becomes periodicity, and a general Type-I ancient limit remains a complete bounded trajectory rather than automatically a fixed point.

A rigidity route to exclude Type-I blow-up factors into (i) rescaling/compactness and nontriviality, (ii) inheritance of a property P by the ancient limit, and (iii) a Liouville theorem saying every ancient solution in class P is trivial.

Critical L3 regularity gives a different sufficient exclusion route: uniform L-infinity_t L3_x control prevents singularity, while a corresponding ancient-solution theorem can force zero from suitable L3 control along times tending to minus infinity.
solved_analogues: Backward Leray self-similar profiles are excluded under the hypotheses of Nečas–Růžička–Šverák (1996), with Tsai (1998) extending the exclusion under broad local-energy-type assumptions.

Koch–Nadirashvili–Seregin–Šverák (2009) prove Liouville results for bounded ancient solutions in 2D and in restricted 3D axisymmetric settings, while explicitly leaving the general 3D bounded-ancient classification open.
near_solved_analogues: Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák (2003) prove regularity under the scale-critical L-infinity_t L3_x condition using backward uniqueness.

Albritton–Barker (2019) reduce local Type-I singularities to nontrivial mild bounded ancient solutions with Type-I decay and prove additional rigidity under stronger scale-critical weak-Lp hypotheses.

explicit_disanalogies: Excluding exact or discrete self-similarity does not exclude a genuinely nonperiodic bounded ancient trajectory.
Excluding all Type-I singularities would still leave Type-II finite-time singularities as an explicit root-level residual.
Scale-invariant boundedness is not the same as critical-norm smallness and is not automatically equivalent across velocity, vorticity, gradient, and pressure formulations.
The 3D Navier–Stokes rescaled flow lacks a known coercive monotonicity formula or critical conserved quantity that would automatically collapse omega-limit sets to equilibria.
Nonlocal pressure and far-field behavior can invalidate naive localization or weak-limit arguments.

Forward self-similar or discretely self-similar Navier–Stokes solutions show that scale invariance alone cannot be treated as a contradiction; the backward-time, energy, integrability, and ancient-solution hypotheses are load-bearing.

periodic orbits encode discrete scale invariance

cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Classify the orbit type and inherited compactness/decay properties of the rescaled Type-I flow before applying any rigidity theorem derived only for stationary profiles.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: In the target PDE, prove the exact rescaled evolution, topology/precompactness, inherited bounds, and either convergence/periodicity or a Liouville theorem for the full resulting trajectory class; a fixed-point-only theorem fails this obligation.
